rejected.title: Mental fitness in sport
card: Mental fitness is the ability to cope with stress, manage emotions and keep a positive outlook. Like physical fitness, it can be built and maintained.
Regular physical activity can support mental fitness. It can lift mood, ease stress and anxiety, and give people a sense of belonging when done with others.
Elite sport adds pressure, such as selection, public criticism, injury and the end of a career. These pressures can harm an athlete's mental health.

Because of this, elite sport pathways have a duty of care to protect athletes' mental health. This can include access to counsellors, education on wellbeing and a culture where athletes feel safe to ask for help.
rejected.remember: Activity can support mental fitness, and elite pathways have a duty to look after athletes' mental health.

a.q: Which statement best describes mental fitness?
opts: The ability to cope with stress and manage emotions
The ability to keep training without ever feeling stress
The ability to win under pressure in elite competition
The absence of any mental health condition for life
a.why: Mental fitness is about coping with stress, managing emotions and keeping a positive outlook, and it can be built over time. It is not freedom from stress, because everyone faces stress and the skill is in coping with it.
a.clue: Think of it as a skill that can be built, like physical fitness.

b.q: Ravi, 17, has joined a state talent academy and is feeling anxious about selection. Which action by the academy best meets its duty of care?
opts: Offer him a counsellor and make it safe to ask for help
Tell him to focus on training and deal with it alone
Drop him from the squad until the anxiety has passed
Give him extra training sessions to take his mind off it
b.why: A duty of care means actively supporting the athlete, such as offering counselling and making it safe to ask for help. Extra training may seem helpful because activity can support mood, but it does not protect his mental health in the face of selection pressure.
b.clue: Which option actively supports the athlete rather than ignoring or removing him?
